note: Frozen canonicalisation vectors for guardian/audit/canonical.py. Every sha256 below is a LITERAL a human wrote down, never a value recomputed by the code under test: ADR-022 makes that the difference between a rule that is enforced and one that merely agrees with itself. guardian/audit/crosscheck.py compares each value against BOTH canonical (the expected bytes) and sha256 (their digest), and additionally against monitor/aggregator/models.py's independent implementation of the same rule -- the Monitor frames its output with a trailing LF and the Guardian does not, so the cross-check compares guardian bytes + LF against the Monitor bytes. Changing any digest here is a deliberate reviewed diff and, after the v1.0 freeze, a hotfix ADR (AGENTS.md iron rule 6). Nothing in this repository regenerates this file.

vectors.why: the degenerate case; two spellings of nothing must not be two digests
an empty list is not an empty object, and the digests say so
clause 5: booleans and null are JSON literals, never 0/1 or the string 'None'
clause 1: ascending code point, so '_' (95) sorts between 'C' (67) and 'a' (97) -- a locale-aware or case-insensitive sort would order these differently
clause 1 again, with a key outside ASCII: sorting is over code points, not over the escaped forms clause 3 later emits
clause 2: no insignificant whitespace at any depth, including inside nested arrays
clause 3: BMP code points leave as \uXXXX, so every emitted byte is ASCII
clause 3 above the BMP: an astral code point is emitted as a surrogate PAIR of escapes, which is the detail a re-implementation is most likely to get wrong
clause 7, first half: U+00E9 as itself. Compare the digest with unicode-nfd-decomposed
clause 7, second half: 'e' + U+0301, which normalises to the vector above and MUST NOT hash to it. An audit record is a transcript, and normalising it would paraphrase evidence
the value ADR-022 names as one the fixture could plausibly have missed: an unpaired surrogate. Clause 3 escapes it, so the emitted bytes stay ASCII and encodable

the escape table: quote, backslash, the C0 controls with short forms, one control without one, and U+2028 which is a JavaScript line terminator but not a JSON one. '/' is NOT escaped, which is a real difference between serialisers

vectors.why: clause 5: 1 and 1.0 are different values and must not collide
clause 5 at the width where a re-implementation backed by a 64-bit integer type would lose precision or switch to a float
clause 5/6: -0.0 is not 0 and not 0.0; the sign survives
clause 6: CPython's shortest round-tripping repr, including the exponent forms

the shared fixture ADR-022's cross-check canonicalises through both implementations: one whole AuditRecord body, minus its hash, in the shape guardian/app/models.py declares -- every field pattern-valid against that module, so the vector is a record the contract would accept and not merely a plausible-looking dictionary
